exposure: different diagnostic criteria for extrauterine growth restriction (EUGR) (cross-sectional, longitudinal, true cross-sectional, true longitudinal)
outcome: concordance among different growth charts and diagnostic criteria
cohort: The study included 7914 extremely-low-birthweight (ELBW) infants from the Spanish SEN1500 Network.
finding: The prevalence of extrauterine growth restriction (EUGR) varied significantly depending on the diagnostic criteria and growth charts used, with Fenton yielding higher prevalence rates, and agreement among charts generally being substantial except for longitudinal EUGR by weight.
